text.tspan: Two triggers, one shared reusable workflow.
Read top to bottom: it is a timeline.

g.text: ② LAUNCHED IMMEDIATELY AT t = 0 — 14 job definitions, not one `needs:` between them
③ THE ONLY JOBS THAT WAIT ON needs:

text.tspan: one job per Codecov flag, each starting when its own tests finish
best-effort, and deliberately NOT wired into the Gate
backend uploads only after green API tests
Codecov backend: patch red under 80%, project red on a drop over 0.2 point
if: always() · timeout 10 min · needs: 19 jobs · Coverage excluded
→ POST rerun-failed-jobs on the same run
Loops back to ② as attempt 2 — exactly once

g.text: LEGEND — HOW TO READ THE ARROWS

text.tspan: CORE vs NIGHTLY — THE ONLY THREE DIFFERENCES
Core: 8 cells — 7 balanced shards + a 'remaining' catch-all, Elasticsearch
Nightly: the same 8 run twice, on Elasticsearch AND OpenSearch
Core: 10 cells, standard image only, chrome/amd64 + chromium/arm64
sharded arsenals / multitenant / remaining, plus 4 infra cells
Nightly: 25 cells, std + ubi9, five browsers, amd64 + arm64
plus the OpenSearch variants and 7 infra cells
Core: reports findings, never blocks the Gate
Nightly: fails the Gate on high/critical findings and scanner errors
timeout 20 min · ESLint + dependency-cruiser + knip + Vitest
timeout 15 min · Spring Boot BOM overrides
timeout 45 min · registry or artifact fallback
needs: — a real dependency declared in the YAML
The consumer will not start until the whole upstream job has finished,
artifact gzip / validate / upload included: ~2.5 min it never reads.
Only six edges in this entire pipeline are true needs:
POLLING WAIT — no needs: in the YAML at all
The consumer starts at t = 0 and boots its services in parallel, then polls
GitHub artifact metadata and producer conclusions every 15 seconds. A successful push
publishes an attempt-scoped marker; only then does the consumer touch GHCR.
Terminal producer failures abort immediately; image artifacts remain the fallback.
LAUNCH — the workflow starting a job. Not a dependency:
these 14 jobs have no upstream and begin the instant the run does.
RETRY LOOP — a separate workflow re-running the failed jobs,
once, and only on the first attempt.
⏱ EVERY DURATION ON A JOB IS ITS timeout-minutes CEILING
It is the point at which GitHub kills the job — NOT how long the job runs.
A job marked "timeout 45 min" normally finishes in a fraction of that.
"poll cap" figures are the same thing for a wait loop: the give-up point.
DOCKER BUILD HAS NO ARROW FROM PREPARE BUNDLED ASSETS
It re-runs the asset preparation inline with upload-artifact: false
instead of waiting, saving ~1.4 min at the head of the critical path.
